clues: This small village sits in hills in southern Australia. It lies north east of the big city of Adelaide.
Summer days here can climb into the mid forties. Winter nights can drop below freezing.
This town was laid out in 1858. A man named Lewis Johnston planned it on land he had bought.
A father gave this place a lasting gift. He named the new town for his own son.
Grape vines grow in the low river soil. Fruit farms mark this hills village near Adelaide.
